summary: Join our Agricultural Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Training Course to learn how to promote sustainability and enhance ecosystem health in agriculture.
lede: Biodiversity in farming supports pollination, soil fertility, water regulation and resilience across food systems. For agricultural planners, NGO and agribusiness staff, conservation professionals and development practitioners, the course provides practical approaches to map ecosystem services, assess biodiversity values and trade-offs, and integrate biodiversity into policies, projects and evaluation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who must weigh productivity, sustainability, and long-term agricultural resilience: Agricultural policymakers and planners setting national or regional strategies. NGO staff working on food security, rural development, or conservation. Agribusiness managers and sustainability officers balancing profit with responsibility. Environmental and conservation professionals addressing ecosystem pressures. Development practitioners designing agriculture and climate-related programs. Extension officers and farmer organization leaders supporting local capacity. CSR managers in agriculture aligning corporate strategy with biodiversity goals. Researchers and academics working on food systems and sustainability. Project officers implementing climate-smart agriculture initiatives. Anyone tasked with integrating biodiversity into agricultural planning.
modules: Introduction to Agricultural Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
Ecosystem Services in Agricultural Policy and Planning
Integrating Biodiversity into Project Design and Evaluation
Climate Change, Resilience, and Ecosystem Services
Risks and Threats to Agricultural Biodiversity
Tools and Frameworks for Ecosystem Service Assessment
Communicating and Advocating for Biodiversity in Agriculture
